The sum and constant multiple rules for double summations state that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}({a}_{ij}+{b}_{ij}) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{ij}+{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{b}_{ij}, \\ {\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}k{a}_{ij} & =k{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{ij}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the sum rule to the given double summation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{15}{\sum }_{j=1}^{16}({a}_{ij}+{b}_{ij}-2) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{15}{\sum }_{j=1}^{16}{a}_{ij}+{\sum }_{i=1}^{15}{\sum }_{j=1}^{16}{b}_{ij}-{\sum }_{i=1}^{15}{\sum }_{j=1}^{16}2 \\  & =300+250-(2{\sum }_{i=1}^{15}{\sum }_{j=1}^{16}1) \\  & =550-2({\sum }_{i=1}^{15}{\sum }_{j=1}^{16}1).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the fact that

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}1=mn,
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}550-2({\sum }_{i=1}^{15}{\sum }_{j=1}^{16}1) & =550-2\cdot (15\cdot 16) \\  & =550-480 \\  & =70.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{15}{\sum }_{j=1}^{16}({a}_{ij}+{b}_{ij}-2)=70.
$$
